title: OCT Biomarkers: Diabetic Retinopathy vs. Age-Related Macular Degeneration
summary: An exhaustive layer-by-layer optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarker reference guide for Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) and Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD). Features high-yield mnemonics, layer-specific structural alterations, fluid dynamics, and clinical differential diagnoses.

content.explanation: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR): 'From Today Check Every Diabetic Having Necklace VMT' | Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD): 'From Today Check Every Drusen Having OS VMT'

sections.title: Exhaustive OCT Biomarker Layer Matrix (DR vs. AMD)

rows: Intra-retinal: Spongiform / Cystoid / non cystoid; Sub-retinal: NSRD
Intra-retinal: Spongiform / Cystoid / non cystoid; Sub-retinal: NSRD; Sub-RPE
NFL / GCL (Nerve Fiber Layer / Ganglion Cell Layer)
Disorganization of the Retinal Inner Layers (DRIL)
Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy (PAMM), Telangectatic Capillary sign (Telcaps)
Pearl Necklace sign, Angular Sign of Henle fiber layer Hyperreflectivity (ASHH)
Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs), Acute Macular Neuroretinopathy (AMN), Foveal neovessels
PhotoReceptors Outer Segment length (PROS length), Photoreceptors loss (IS / OS, EZ)

Photoreceptors loss (IS / OS, EZ), Disorganization of the Retinal Outer Layers (DROL), Outer Retinal Tubulation (ORT), Sub-retinal Hyper Reflective Material (SHRM), Sub-retinal Drusenoid Deposits (SDD)
Drusen: Size, Calcification; Double Layer Sign (DLS) / Shallow Irregular RPE Elevation (SIRE) (≥ 1000 µ & ≤ 100 µ); RPE Tear

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis of Core OCT Biomarkers

branches: Hyper Reflective Foci (HRF): Microaneurysms, Extravasated Lipoproteins/Lipid Exudates, Activated Microglia, Migrated RPE Pigment Cells
Sub-retinal Hyper Reflective Material (SHRM): Macular Neovascularization (MNV Type 2), Fibrotic Scarring, Subretinal Hemorrhage, Fibrin / Exudative Fluid
PAMM vs. AMN: PAMM = INL hyperreflectivity (Deep Vascular Plexus ischemia); AMN = ONL/OPL hyperreflectivity (Radial Subfoveal Capillary Network ischemia)
Double Layer Sign (DLS / SIRE): Sub-RPE Type 1 MNV, Pachychoroid Neovasculopathy (PNV), Central Serous Chorioretinopathy (CSCR), Drusenoid PED

Outer Retinal Tubulation (ORT): Degenerating Photoreceptors rearranged in circular formations in late-stage AMD, Subretinal Fibrosis, Choroideremia, RP (Do NOT confuse with active Intra-retinal Fluid)

sections.title: Inner & Mid-Retinal Layer Biomarkers (ILM to OPL)
content: ILM Layer: Vitreomacular Adhesion (VMA) and Vitreomacular Traction (VMT) present in both DR and AMD.
NFL / GCL: Disorganization of the Retinal Inner Layers (DRIL) — Key prognostic biomarker in Diabetic Retinopathy predicting visual acuity recovery.
INL Layer (DR): Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy (PAMM) and Telangectatic Capillary sign (Telcaps).
OPL Layer (DR & AMD): Pearl Necklace sign (present in DR & AMD); Angular Sign of Henle fiber layer Hyperreflectivity (ASHH) (DR specific).
Pan-Retinal (All Layers): Hyper Reflective Foci (HRF) observed across both DR and AMD.

sections.title: Outer Retinal & Photoreceptor Biomarkers (ONL, ELM, PRL)
content: ONL Layer (DR Specific): Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs), Acute Macular Neuroretinopathy (AMN), and Foveal neovessels.
ELM Layer: External Limiting Membrane (ELM) disruption — CRITICAL biomarker for photoreceptor integrity in DR.
PRL Layer (DR): PhotoReceptors Outer Segment length (PROS length) & Photoreceptor loss (IS / OS junction, Ellipsoid Zone [EZ]).

PRL Layer (AMD Specific): Photoreceptor loss (IS / OS, EZ), Disorganization of the Retinal Outer Layers (DROL), Outer Retinal Tubulation (ORT), Sub-retinal Hyper Reflective Material (SHRM), and Sub-retinal Drusenoid Deposits (SDD / Reticular Pseudodrusen).

sections.title: RPE & Choroidal Biomarkers
content: RPE Pathology (AMD Specific): Drusen characterized by Size and Calcification; Double Layer Sign (DLS) / Shallow Irregular RPE Elevation (SIRE) (≥ 1000 µ width & ≤ 100 µ height); RPE Tear.
Choroidal Morphology (DR): Choroidal Thickness changes (Thinned in advanced ischemia, altered in DME).

Choroidal Morphology (AMD): Choroidal Thickness changes & Prechoroidal Cleft (a hyporeflective space between sub-RPE material and Bruch's membrane indicating high risk for RPE tear or active neovascularization).

sections.title: Retinal Fluid Distribution & Macular Profile
content: Central Retinal Thickness (CRT): Quantitative metric utilized for treatment response tracking in both DR and AMD.
Intra-retinal Fluid (IRF): Spongiform / Cystoid / Non-cystoid intraretinal edema observed in both DR and AMD.
Sub-retinal Fluid (SRF): Non-Sensory Retinal Detachment (NSRD) present in both DR and AMD.
Sub-RPE Fluid / Elevation: Exclusively mapped under AMD pathology (e.g., Fibrovascular / Serous PED).

sections.title: Clinical Red Flags & Prognostic High-Risk Indicators
content: Prechoroidal Cleft in AMD: High structural stress indicator, strongly predicting imminent RPE Tear or active non-responding Type 1/3 MNV.
DRIL > 500 µm in DR: Strong clinical predictor of poor visual acuity gain despite resolution of macular edema.
Sub-retinal Hyper Reflective Material (SHRM): Associated with incomplete anti-VEGF response, rapid photoreceptor loss, and progression to subretinal fibrosis.
Outer Retinal Tubulation (ORT): Represents dead-end photoreceptor rearrangement. Do NOT misinterpret as intraretinal fluid (IRF) and overtreat with anti-VEGF injections.
